name: cardiac_dirchange_v3_benchmark_v1
description: Direction-change troponin benchmark (v3) — full-EHR context. Each case has a visible troponin trend that REVERSES at the target time. Tests whether agents use cross-lab signals rather than troponin trend extrapolation. Full EHR includes: demographics, ethnicity, race, diagnosis descriptions, medication names, procedures, observations/vitals, visit history.

design.why_hard: Both last-value and trend-extrapolation heuristics fail by construction. Agents must use cross-lab gap signals to detect the reversal. Full-EHR context provides comprehensive patient data but does not contain the answer.
design.lab_timeline_note: lab_timeline includes all labs up to t_target EXCEPT troponin after t_visible. Rows with in_gap=True are from the gap window (t_visible < t <= t_target).

conditions.control: Full EHR + PubMed MCP Server access
conditions.independent: Full EHR only (no PubMed MCP Server)

question.stem:
Patient subject_id: 115968758

A 48-year-old Male presents with chest symptoms. Current diagnoses: 572.2; 789.59; 511.9; 570; 578.9; 793.1; V45.89; 038.44. Current medications: not recorded.

The lab timeline below shows measurements up to 2009-09-29T11:45. IMPORTANT: Troponin I measurements are only available up to 2009-09-27T12:20 (11 troponin readings visible). The visible troponin trend is rising (most recent readings increasing >20%). Non-troponin labs (creatinine, BNP, etc.) continue to be available up to 2009-09-29T11:45 and are included in the timeline — use them to detect any change in the troponin trajectory.

The next Troponin I measurement is scheduled for 2009-09-29T11:45 (47.4 hours after the last known troponin reading).

Based on this patient's full lab history and cross-lab signals during the gap window, predict the Troponin I value at 2009-09-29T11:45.

scoring_guide.note: Score = direction_correct (0.4 if direction matches, else 0) + within_50pct (0.35 if |error| <= 50%, else 0) + within_20pct (0.25 if |error| <= 20%, else 0). Max = 1.0. Note: direction_correct uses the reversed direction (the actual direction at target), NOT the visible trend — both last-value and trend-extrapolation heuristics fail by design.
